findings.title: OIDCbaselineconfusesIDtokenandAccessToken
findings.impact: Bounded OIDC baseline-token-role and compatibility-description defect. Section 3.2 explicitly assumes customized registration and new delegation credentials; no specific authentication or non-escalation inference of that customized design is shown to require ID-token use as the UserInfo access credential.
findings.counterevidence: Section 3.2 customizes registration and introduces new delegation credentials; Figure 2 explicitly incorporates new delegation mechanisms. Additional tokeninfo or delegation-validation services can be specified by such an extension. These qualifications do not make ID-token-to-UserInfo a Core behavior.
findings.dependency: Section 3.1 ordinary-provider flow motivates Section 3.2, but the latter expressly adds a credential/registration extension. The standard-OP wording requires an explicit extended-provider validation profile. Core-only support is insufficient; the proposal does not supply or claim a fully specified unchanged-Core validator.
findings.severity_rationale: Minor on the demonstrated local protocol-description scope, with operative extension qualifications preserved. Neither absence of an exploit, survival of every realization, nor position-paper status is used as the severity criterion.

acceptance_calibration.change: Corrected severity rationale only; supported finding severity unchanged.
